description: §6.7.1a — an EXPRESSION-position `match` inside an `on mount { }` body: `let y = match @n { … }`. The match parses to a `match-expr` NESTED under the `let`, never a top-level statement, so detection must recurse into the statement node (S313 review #2 — a top-level-kind check misses it). Pre-fix bc51b610 fails E-CODEGEN-INVALID-LOGIC; post-fix @n = 2 selects the `2` arm, y = "two", and @label = y. No input — the boot/mount shape.
rationale: §6.7.1a sugar-equivalence — an expression-position `match` (a `match-expr` bound by a `let`) inside `on mount` lowers exactly as inside a `function` body. With @n = 2 the literal-2 arm is selected, so y = "two" and @label = "two".
